evidence.title: SOP-07 Solvent cleaning of dispersers and mixing vessels
evidence.claim: In 2015, the waiting time before the next charge was restored to 60 minutes, reversing a previous reduction.
evidence.quote: Wait before next charge restored to 60 min (CR-2015-004 cancels CR-2014-011).

evidence.title: SOP-07 Solvent cleaning of dispersers and mixing vessels
evidence.claim: In 2014, the waiting time before the next charge was reduced to 15 minutes.
evidence.quote: Wait before next charge reduced to 15 min (CR-2014-011).

evidence.title: SOP-07 Solvent cleaning of dispersers and mixing vessels
evidence.claim: In 1998, a 60-minute wait was required to ensure acetone vapors cleared before hot charging.
evidence.quote: Wait 60 min before charging next batch (acetone vapour must clear before hot charge).

evidence.title: Change request CR-2015-004
evidence.claim: In 2015, the 60-minute wait was restored because residual acetone and hot charging caused flammable atmospheres and film defects.
evidence.quote: residual acetone vapour combined with hot charging gives a flammable atmosphere and film defects.

evidence.title: Deviation report DR-2015-006
evidence.claim: In 2015, charging AF-12 hot only 15 minutes after acetone cleaning caused LEL alarms and film defects (popping and craters).
evidence.quote: LEL alarm at 35 % during charging; the batch showed popping and craters attributed to residual acetone.

evidence.title: Change request CR-2014-011
evidence.claim: In 2014, the waiting time was reduced from 60 to 15 minutes to increase production capacity after successful trials on D-1 and D-2.
evidence.quote: reduce the wait after cleaning from 60 to 15 minutes to gain capacity (about 1,000 vessel-hours per year).

evidence.claim: In 2012, staff discussed the purpose of leaving lids open overnight and noted the existing 60-minute wait for acetone vapor clearance.
evidence.quote: we wait 60 min and ventilate before entry now anyway

verdict.process_name: SOP-07 solvent cleaning of dispersers and mixing vessels
verdict.instruction: Wait at least 60 min after cleaning before charging the next batch.
verdict.reason: The 60-minute wait is required to clear acetone vapors before hot charging to prevent flammable atmospheres (LEL alarms) and product quality defects (popping and craters), as documented after a failed reduction to 15 minutes.

chain.claim: A 60-minute wait was established to ensure acetone vapors clear before hot charging
Reducing the wait to 15 minutes caused LEL alarms and film defects (popping and craters)
The 60-minute wait was restored in 2015 to mitigate these hazards

dependencies.name: acetone vapour combined with hot charging
dependencies.note: Hazard persists if wait time is reduced

counter_evidence.claim: Wait time was reduced to 15 minutes to increase capacity
counter_evidence.resolution: Reversed in 2015 due to safety and quality failures
